text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game with a negative externality twist: each private token nets me +1 but costs others 0.3 each, while each group token only gives me +0.3 but presumably benefits the group collectively. I'm working through the exact payoff structure to figure out which allocation actually maximizes my score versus the group's.

Working out the math: if group payoff benefits everyone, full cooperation yields 24 points each versus only 2 if everyone keeps private tokens — a classic social dilemma where collective welfare favors contributing but individual incentive favors defecting. Given the ambiguity in how group tokens pay out, I'll lean toward cooperating early to test the waters and signal good faith, settling on contributing 20 tokens to the group this round.
